evidence: Phase406 writer-visible packet represented the clerk identity semantically/romanized as Wu Lan rather than as an immutable Chinese literal.
The fresh writer had to reconstruct the Chinese name during free language generation.
The output produced a plausible homophonic Chinese character substitution: 兰 -> 岚.
No evidence indicates the character identity itself was intentionally changed at the story-model level.
causal_diagnosis.distinction: This is a lexical identity fidelity failure, not a general prose-quality, dialogue, pacing or style failure.

rejected_repairs: tell writer to be more careful with names
retry until spelling happens to match
lock ordinary nouns or prose wording
expand into a global surface-style rule

selected_architecture.mechanism: Provide canonical hard identities as exact Chinese literal tokens in a separate immutable binding table. Semantic character records reference identity IDs, while any emitted explicit name must be copied from the canonical literal rather than reconstructed from romanization or semantics.
selected_architecture.scope: Only hard identity tokens and similarly exact proper-name literals explicitly designated by source authority.
writer_freedom_preserved: whether to use the proper name or a natural pronoun/reference where source-consistent
all surrounding syntax, rhythm, paragraphing, dialogue and narration
forbidden: phonetic reconstruction of a bound identity

validation_limit: A single Phase407 A1 can show one bounded hard-identity preservation signal only; it cannot prove universal proper-name fidelity.
